question: In △ABC, at point D, BD ⟂ AC and ∠DBC = 33°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 70°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right triangle BDC, angle C = 90° − angle DBC

Angle C = 90° − 33° = 57°

Apply Exterior Angle Theorem in triangle AEC

Angle AEB = angle CAE + angle C

**∴ Answer = 70° + 57° = 127°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In triangle ABC, BD ⟂ AC ⇒ angle BDC = 90°

Angle DBC = 33° and angle CAE = 70°

Point E lies on BC

**Formula used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

Exterior angle = sum of opposite interior angles

 
 
• 
• 
 
 33° 
 70° 
 ? A D C B E 

 

Calculation:

⇒ In right triangle BDC:

⇒ angle BDC + angle DBC + angle BCD = 180°

⇒ 90° + 33° + angle BCD = 180°

⇒ angle BCD = 180° − 123° = 57°

⇒ Since A, D, C are collinear ⇒ angle ACE = angle BCD = 57°

⇒ Now in triangle AEC:

⇒ angle CAE = 70°

⇒ Using exterior angle property:

⇒ angle AEB = angle CAE + angle ACE

⇒ angle AEB = 70° + 57°

⇒ angle AEB = 127°

∴ The correct answer is 127°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its two opposite interior angles. Formula: Exterior angle = sum of opposite interior angles

Angle Sum Property

In any triangle: angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°

Right Triangle Property

If one angle is 90°, the remaining two angles sum to 90°

Linear Pair

Two adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180°
